thread.title: Chinese biotech stocks hit by a double whammy, which means it’s time to buy

author: Michael Brush
title: Chinese biotech stocks hit by a double whammy, which means it’s time to buy
text:
Have investors hit peak negativity on China-based companies? I think there’s a good chance they have. If so, it’s time to buy China stocks, especially in biotechnology.
Chinese biotech stocks have been particularly hammered because they are getting hit by a double whammy. They’re down because investors are overly negative on China due to trade-war tensions. And unlike the S&P 500 Index SPX, +0.82% the U.S. biotech sector is actually already in a bear market. The SPDR S&P Biotech exchange traded fund XBI, +1.49% was recently down 25% from its summer highs.
I’ll tell you the best way to buy China biotech stocks — and it is surprisingly easy. But first let’s look at why the worries behind the selloff in China stocks and biotech in general are overblown.
On China fears, it’s key to keep in mind that President Donald Trump’s negotiating style is to start with bluster (which spooks investors) and then dial back to compromise to be able to boast about a “deal.”
That’s going to be the case with China trade. One reason is that, near term, neither country can stand — or deserves — the pain that comes from a harsh trade regime.
U.S. companies have extensive supply chains winding through China, which will be hard and costly to replace. U.S. consumers enjoy the cheap, yet high-quality, goods that come out of China — everything from guitars to Apple AAPL, -0.54% iPhones. China needs U.S. markets and access to U.S. business partnerships, and university slots for students.
So we’re going to see signs of progress on China trade talks and probably soon — at the G20 summit in Buenos Aires Nov. 30 through Dec. 1.
“The majority of clients believe there will be a truce, meaning there will be an agreement to resume negotiations and there will be no increase in tariffs over that period,” says John Normand, head of cross-asset fundamental strategy at J.P. Morgan Chase JPM, +1.03%
Even if we don’t get any signs of progress on China trade tensions, it never made sense that China biotech stocks should get hit by this war on trade. After all, who would hold human lives hostage to politics?
On the biotech weakness, the key thing to remember here is that the selloff has little to do with sector trends, says Jefferies biotech analyst Michael Yee. It’s more about investors fleeing a high-beta group in a risk-off environment. When investor confidence returns, which is likely because there’s no looming recession and because the Fed will probably soon signal it’s reducing the number of planned rate hikes, high-beta groups like biotech will be among the best performers. China biotech stocks look like a great way to position for this kind of move, given the double whammy at work.
But how to get access? Here you’re in luck. For the past few years biotech expert Brad Loncar has been travelling to China to meet with biotech companies and study which ones to put in a China biotech index he’s devised. Now there’s a an ETF based on that index. It’s called the Loncar China BioPharma ETF CHNA, +1.47%
Loncar got a big break in this effort when Hong Kong recently loosened listing standards for companies, in that they’re no longer required to show revenue. This opened the door to listings of China biotech companies on the Hong Kong exchange. That’s a good thing for investors, because the Hong Kong exchange has fairly stringent listing standards. Mistakes will get through, but this generally means investors are less likely to buy into a fraud when they buy a Hong Kong-listed China biotech stock.
The Loncar China BioPharma ETF gives you easy access to 28 biotech companies. Based on a small sampling of this group that I’ve studied and suggested in my stock newsletter, Brush Up on Stocks , these are quality companies with decent prospects. One of them is BeiGene BGNE, +6.53% which I first suggested in my letter at $28 in February 2016. It was up 685% by June 2018. And even in the biotech rout it is still up 400%. (My current buy limit is $100, give or take a little.) Another of mine in the Loncar ETF is the small-cap CASI Pharmaceuticals CASI, +10.74% This one advanced 270% after I suggested it in the low $2 range in early November 2017. I recently reiterated it because it looks attractive again in the pullback below $4.
The Loncar China BioPharma ETF gives you access to plenty more potential China biotech winners like these, but it has one shortcoming, at least for now. Volume and liquidity are low, which means the bid-ask spread is wide. One way around this is to put in a limit buy order near the bid, and camp out until it gets hit.
Besides an expected truce in the war on trade with China, which will soon put a bid under Chinese stocks again, here are four other reasons why it makes sense to invest in Chinese biotech for the long haul.
1. The government really wants the sector to win
Until recently, China had no biotech or pharma sector speak of. Most pharma companies either developed generic drugs or manufactured drugs. “They didn’t do innovation or create new drugs, but that is changing dramatically overnight,” says Loncar. Biotech is a key part of the country’s efforts to spur continued growth by developing more sophisticated companies.
2. The Hong Kong exchange now welcomes revenue-light businesses from China
“That basically describes 99% of biotech companies,” Loncar, because they tend to be early-stage, developing businesses. The Hong Kong change is “huge” for China’s biotech sector, says Loncar, because it gives venture-capital firms an easier way to exit investments to realize gains, and put the money into start-ups. “That is super-important because it creates an ecosystem for investing in biotech for the first time,” says Loncar.
3. China FDA upgrade
China has completely revamped its version of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), to bring it up to global standards, says Loncar. This improves the quality of the sector, and piques investor interest.
4. U.S.-trained talent is returning home
Major China companies including Tencent TCEHY, +0.91% Baidu BIDU, +2.76% and Alibaba BABA, +2.93% exist, in part, because Chinese nationals who studied in the U.S. and worked at U.S. companies like Google GOOG, +0.56% GOOGL, +1.38% Facebook FB, +1.39% and Amazon.com AMZN, +0.99% returned to China to work in tech start-ups.
“A lot of Chinese professionals who were educated in the U.S. and worked at U.S. biotech companies are going home now and starting biotech companies,” says Loncar.
Those four factors add up to a “perfect storm” that should create a solid biotech sector in the country over the next several years. If so, now is the time to buy in.
Keep in mind that even if these stocks get a boost near term on signs of progress in U.S.-China trade talks, this group will be volatile because U.S.-China tensions will persist for decades as the two great powers battle for global hegemony.
But there may be some good news in this, too. Persistent trade tensions could increase China’s focus on developing its biotech sector, as a way to move away from reliance on trade for growth, says Loncar. “They’re going to have world-class biotech sector, I have no doubt about that.”
At the time of publication, Michael Brush had no positions in any stocks mentioned in this column. Brush has suggested BGNE and CASI in his stock newsletter, Brush Up on Stocks . Brush is a Manhattan-based financial writer who has covered business for the New York Times and The Economist Group, and he attended Columbia Business School in the Knight-Bagehot program.
